`parse_ovation_aurora` also takes `partial=False`; `True` accepts a grid
with whole longitudes missing.

## Client

`from swpc_kit.client import Client, AsyncClient` (`client` extra).

`Client(*, transport: Transport | None = None, user_agent: str = 'swpc-kit/0.1.0 (+https://github.com/Tabrigos/swpc-kit)', timeout: float = 30.0, max_age: timedelta | None = None, conditional: bool = True, clock: Callable[[], datetime] = _utc_now) -> None`

`AsyncClient` takes the same arguments, its methods are coroutines, and it
closes with `aclose()` / `async with`.

- `fetch(product: Product[M], *, max_age: timedelta | None = None) -> M`: Fetch and parse `product` (one of `PRODUCTS`).
- `close() -> None`: Close the transport.
- one method per product, `client.<method>(*, max_age=None) -> Model` (see [Products](#products)).

## Models: solar_wind

`swpc_kit.models.solar_wind` (all re-exported by `swpc_kit.models`).

### `RtswMag1m`

One-minute interplanetary magnetic field of the last 24 hours.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | `tuple[RtswMagSample, ...]` | The records of every source, oldest first; records with the same time keep the order of the source file. |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `active_at(time: datetime) -> Optional[S]`: Return the active record at exactly `time`, or `None`.
- `active_series() -> tuple[S, ...]`: Return the active record of each time that has one, oldest first.
- `data_time` → `datetime`: Time of the most recent record, from any source.
- `latest_active() -> Optional[S]`: Return the most recent active record, or `None` if there is none.
- `series(source: str) -> tuple[S, ...]`: Return the records of `source`, oldest first (empty if none).
- `sources` → `tuple[str, ...]`: Names of the sources in the content, sorted.

### `RtswMagSample`

One one-minute record of the interplanetary magnetic field.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `time` | `datetime` | Time of the record. Not always on the minute (IMAP). |
| `source` | `str` | Spacecraft, such as `"SOLAR1"` (see `RtswSource`). |
| `active` | `bool` | Whether this source is the one SWPC uses at this time. |

## Models: goes

`swpc_kit.models.goes` (all re-exported by `swpc_kit.models`).

### `FlareClass`

A solar flare class, such as `M2.5` (a flux of 2.5e-5 W/m²).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `letter` | `str` | `"A"`, `"B"`, `"C"`, `"M"` or `"X"`. |
| `multiplier` | `float` | Flux divided by the lower bound of the letter's decade, 0 to 9.9 for A to M, 0 or more for X. |

- `flux` → `float`: The flux the class stands for, in W/m² (M2.5 is 2.5e-5).
- `from_flux(flux: float) -> FlareClass`: Return the class of a 0.1-0.8 nm flux in W/m².

### `GoesIntegralProtons`

GOES integral proton flux above each energy threshold.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | `tuple[ProtonSample, ...]` | The values of every threshold, oldest first; values with the same time keep the order of the source file. |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `data_time` → `datetime`: Time of the most recent value, of any threshold.
- `latest(threshold_mev: float) -> ProtonSample | None`: Return the most recent value above `threshold_mev`, or `None`.
- `series(threshold_mev: float) -> tuple[ProtonSample, ...]`: Return the values above `threshold_mev`, oldest first.
- `thresholds` → `tuple[float, ...]`: The energy thresholds in the content, in MeV, ascending.

### `GoesXrays`

GOES X-ray flux in both bands.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | `tuple[XraySample, ...]` | The values of every band, oldest first; values with the same time keep the order of the source file. |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `band(energy: str) -> tuple[XraySample, ...]`: Return the values of one band, oldest first (empty if none).
- `data_time` → `datetime`: Time of the most recent value, of any band.
- `energies` → `tuple[str, ...]`: The bands in the content, sorted.
- `latest(energy: str = XrayBand.LONG) -> XraySample | None`: Return the most recent value of a band, or `None`.
- `peak(energy: str = XrayBand.LONG) -> XraySample | None`: Return the value of a band with the highest flux, or `None`.

### `ProtonSample`

One GOES integral proton flux value above one energy threshold.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `time` | `datetime` | Time of the value. |
| `satellite` | `int` | GOES satellite number, such as 18. |
| `energy` | `str` | Threshold as written in the source, such as `">=10 MeV"`. |
| `threshold_mev` | `float` | The threshold in MeV, such as 10.0. |
| `flux` | `float \| None` | Integral flux in pfu (particles cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹), or `None`. |

### `XrayBand`

The two GOES X-ray bands, as written in the `energy` field.

Members: `SHORT` = `'0.05-0.4nm'`, `LONG` = `'0.1-0.8nm'`.

### `XraySample`

One GOES X-ray flux value of one band.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `time` | `datetime` | Time of the value. |
| `satellite` | `int` | GOES satellite number, such as 18. |
| `energy` | `str` | Band, such as `"0.1-0.8nm"` (see `XrayBand`). |
| `flux` | `float \| None` | Flux in W/m², after the electron correction, or `None`. |
| `observed_flux` | `float \| None` | Flux in W/m² before the correction, or `None`. |
| `electron_correction` | `float \| None` | Correction subtracted, in W/m², or `None`. |
| `electron_contamination` | `bool \| None` | Whether the value is flagged as contaminated by electrons (`electron_contaminaton`, so spelled, in the source), or `None`. |

- `flare_class` → `FlareClass | None`: Flare class of the flux, for the 0.1-0.8 nm band only.

## Models: alerts

`swpc_kit.models.alerts` (all re-exported by `swpc_kit.models`).

### `AlertMessage`

One space weather message (alert, warning, watch or summary).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `product_id` | `str` | Short code of the message, such as `"K04W"`. |
| `code` | `str` | Long code from the `Space Weather Message Code:` line, such as `"WARK04"`. |
| `serial_number` | `int` | From the `Serial Number:` line. Not unique: a continued alert can repeat the serial number of an earlier one. |
| `issued` | `datetime` | `issue_datetime` of the record, to the millisecond. |
| `issue_time` | `datetime` | From the `Issue Time:` line, to the minute. |
| `kind` | `MessageKind \| None` | Kind of message from its title, or `None` when unknown. |
| `title` | `str` | The title line (`"ALERT: Geomagnetic K-index of 5"`), or an empty string when the message has none. |
| `valid_from` | `datetime \| None` | `Valid From:`, or `None`. |
| `valid_to` | `datetime \| None` | `Now Valid Until:` (extended warnings) or `Valid To:`, or `None`. |
| `threshold_reached` | `datetime \| None` | `Threshold Reached:`, or `None`. |
| `begin_time` | `datetime \| None` | `Begin Time:`, or `None`. |
| `maximum_time` | `datetime \| None` | `Maximum Time:` or `Max time:`, or `None`. |
| `end_time` | `datetime \| None` | `End Time:`, or `None`. |
| `observed` | `datetime \| None` | `Observed:` (sudden impulse summaries), or `None`. |
| `extension_to_serial` | `int \| None` | `Extension to Serial Number:`, or `None`. |
| `continuation_of_serial` | `int \| None` | `Continuation of Serial Number:`, or `None`. |
| `cancel_serial` | `int \| None` | `Cancel Serial Number:`, or `None`. |
| `noaa_scale` | `NoaaScale \| None` | First valid `NOAA Scale:` or `Noaa Scale:`, or `None`. Watches give their level in the title, not here. |
| `fields` | `tuple[MessageField, ...]` | Every `Name: value` line after the title, in order, repeats included. A typed attribute is `None` when its value has an unknown form; the raw value stays here. |
| `text` | `str` | The message as served. |

- `field(name: str) -> str | None`: Return the value of the first field called `name`, or `None`.
- `info` → `MessageCode | None`: Catalogue entry of the message, by short code then long code.

### `Alerts`

The space weather messages of the last weeks (`alerts.json`).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `tuple[AlertMessage, ...]` | The messages, in source order (newest first). May be empty. |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `data_time` → `datetime | None`: Issue time of the most recent message, or `None` when empty.

### `MessageField`

One `Name: value` line of the body of a message.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | The name as written, such as `"Valid From"`. |
| `value` | `str` | The rest of the line, without surrounding spaces; may be empty. |

### `MessageKind`

The kind of a message, from the word before the colon of its title.

Members: `ALERT` = `'ALERT'`, `CONTINUED_ALERT` = `'CONTINUED ALERT'`, `WARNING` = `'WARNING'`, `EXTENDED_WARNING` = `'EXTENDED WARNING'`, `WATCH` = `'WATCH'`, `CANCEL_WATCH` = `'CANCEL WATCH'`, `SUMMARY` = `'SUMMARY'`.

### `NoaaScale`

A NOAA scale level, as in `NOAA Scale: G1 - Minor`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `category` | `ScaleCategory` | Which scale. |
| `level` | `int` | Level from 1 to 5. |
| `label` | `str \| None` | The word after the level, such as `"Minor"`, or `None`. SWPC writes `"Greater"` for "this level or greater". |

- `code` → `str`: The level as letter and number, such as `"G1"`.

### `ScaleCategory`

The three NOAA space weather scales, by their letter.

Members: `GEOMAGNETIC_STORM` = `'G'`, `SOLAR_RADIATION_STORM` = `'S'`, `RADIO_BLACKOUT` = `'R'`.

### `field_key(name: str) -> str`

Return `name` normalised for comparing field names.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `day` | `date` | The UTC day. |
| `ap` | `int` | The Ap index. |

### `GeomagneticForecast`

The geomagnetic forecast: Ap, storm probabilities and Kp.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `issued` | `datetime` | The `:Issued:` time. |
| `observed_ap` | `DailyAp` | Ap observed on the day before `estimated_ap`. |
| `estimated_ap` | `DailyAp` | Ap estimated for the day of issue. |
| `days` | `tuple[date, ...]` | The three forecast days. |
| `predicted_ap` | `tuple[DailyAp, ...]` | Ap predicted for each of `days`. |
| `active` | `tuple[int, ...]` | Probability of active conditions, in percent, per day. |
| `minor_storm` | `tuple[int, ...]` | Probability of a minor storm, in percent, per day. |
| `moderate_storm` | `tuple[int, ...]` | Probability of a moderate storm, in percent, per day. |
| `strong_extreme_storm` | `tuple[int, ...]` | Probability of a strong to extreme storm, in percent, per day. |
| `kp` | `tuple[KpPeriod, ...]` | Kp forecast for every 3-hour interval of `days`, in time order. |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `data_time` → `datetime`: The `:Issued:` time.

### `KpPeriod`

One 3-hour interval of a Kp forecast table.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `datetime` | Start of the interval. |
| `kp` | `float` | Kp in thirds, as a decimal (2.67 is 3-), from 0 to 9. |
| `noaa_scale` | `str \| None` | NOAA geomagnetic storm level written next to the value, such as `"G1"` for `5.33 (G1)`, or `None`. |

- `end` → `datetime`: End of the interval, three hours after `start`.

### `OutlookDay`

One day of the 27-day outlook.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `day` | `date` | The UTC day. |
| `radio_flux` | `float` | Predicted 10.7 cm radio flux, in solar flux units. |
| `ap` | `int` | Predicted planetary A index. |
| `largest_kp` | `int` | Predicted largest Kp of the day, from 0 to 9. |

The 3-day forecast: geomagnetic activity, radiation storms, blackouts.

## Models: grids

`swpc_kit.models.grids` (all re-exported by `swpc_kit.models`).

### `DrapFrequencies`

D-RAP: D-region absorption, as a frequency on a global grid.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `grid` | `Grid` | Frequencies in MHz, on a 2 by 4 degree grid. |
| `valid_at` | `datetime` | `Product Valid At` of the source. |
| `estimated_recovery_time` | `str \| None` | `Estimated Recovery Time`, as written (for example `"No Estimate"`). |
| `xray_message` | `str \| None` | `X-RAY Message`. |
| `xray_warning` | `str \| None` | `X-RAY Warning`. |
| `proton_message` | `str \| None` | `Proton Message`. |
| `proton_warning` | `str \| None` | `Proton Warning`. |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `data_time` → `datetime`: The time the product is valid at.
- `times` → `dict[str, datetime]`: `valid_at`.

### `Grid`

Values on a regular latitude/longitude grid, at cell centres.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `latitudes` | `tuple[float, ...]` | Cell-centre latitudes in degrees north, strictly increasing (south to north), within [-90, 90]. |
| `longitudes` | `tuple[float, ...]` | Cell-centre longitudes in degrees east, strictly increasing, within [-180, 360), as the source delivers them. |
| `latitude_step` | `float` | Height of a cell in degrees. |
| `longitude_step` | `float` | Width of a cell in degrees. |
| `values` | `tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]` | One row per latitude, in the order of `latitudes`; each row has one value per longitude, in the order of `longitudes`. |
| `quantity` | `str` | What the values are, such as `"aurora"`. |
| `units` | `str` | Units of the values, such as `"MHz"`. |

- `cells() -> Iterator[tuple[float, float, float]]`: Yield `(latitude, longitude, value)` for every cell, row by row.
- `is_contiguous` → `bool`: Whether both axes have no gaps between their first and last value.
- `shape` → `tuple[int, int]`: Number of latitudes and of longitudes.
- `value_at(latitude: float, longitude: float) -> float`: Return the value of the cell centred at `latitude`, `longitude`.
- `wrapped() -> Grid`: Return the same grid with longitudes in [-180, 180).

### `GridProduct`

A product made of a grid and the times its content declares.

- `data_time` → `datetime`: The time the data describes, in UTC.
- `grid` → `Grid`: The values and their axes.
- `source_url` → `str`: Where the content came from.
- `times` → `Mapping[str, datetime]`: Every time the content declares, by name, in UTC.

### `OvationAurora`

The OVATION aurora nowcast: a global 1-degree grid.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `grid` | `Grid` | The values, with longitudes 0 to 359 as delivered. |
| `observation_time` | `datetime` | `Observation Time` of the source. |
| `forecast_time` | `datetime` | `Forecast Time` of the source (about an hour after the observation). |
| `source_url` | `str` | Where the content came from. |

- `data_time` → `datetime`: The observation time.
- `times` → `dict[str, datetime]`: `observation_time` and `forecast_time`.

### `wrap_longitude(longitude: float) -> float`

Return `longitude` in degrees east, moved into [-180, 180).

## Errors

`from swpc_kit import SwpcError, SourceNotReady, UnexpectedContent, ParseError, StaleData`

- `SwpcError` (Exception): Base class for every error raised by swpc-kit.
- `SourceNotReady` (SwpcError): The data is truncated or empty.
- `UnexpectedContent` (SwpcError): The source answered with something other than the expected product.
- `ParseError` (SwpcError): The format is the expected one, but a value is inconsistent.
- `StaleData` (SwpcError): The data is older than the maximum age the caller accepts.

`ParseError` has `field`, `line` (1-based, text products) and `index`
(0-based record in a JSON array). `StaleData` has `data_time`, `max_age`, `age`.

## Exports

- `swpc_kit.export.to_geojson(product: GridProduct, *, threshold: float | None = None, geometry: Literal['polygon', 'point'] = 'polygon') -> dict[str, Any]`: Return the cells of a gridded product as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection.
- `swpc_kit.export.geotiff.write_geotiff(product, path, *, nodata=nan)` (`geo` extra): write a single-band float32 GeoTIFF in EPSG:4326 with the times in its tags.

## Message codes

`swpc_kit.codes`: catalogue of the alert codes.

- `by_short(code: str) -> MessageCode | None`: Return the entry with short code `code` (e.g. `K04W`), or `None`.
- `by_long(code: str) -> MessageCode | None`: Return the entry with long code `code` (e.g. `WARK04`), or `None`.
- `lookup(code: str) -> MessageCode | None`: Return the entry with `code` as its short or long code, or `None`.

### `MessageCode`

One kind of space weather message.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `long` | `str` | Long code, as in `Space Weather Message Code:`, e.g. `WARK04`. |
| `short` | `str \| None` | Short code, as in the `product_id` of `alerts.json`, e.g. `K04W`; `None` when not known. |
| `meaning` | `str` | What the message announces, e.g. `"Warning: Geomagnetic K-index of 4 expected"`. |
| `scale` | `str \| None` | NOAA scale level the message is about, e.g. `"G1"`, or `None` when the message has no scale level. |
| `verification` | `Verification` | Whether the entry was verified or deduced. |

### `Verification`

How a catalogue entry is known.

Members: `VERIFIED` = `'verified'`, `DEDUCED` = `'deduced'`.
